summary.text: 说 means “speak” or “say.” It is the standardized simplified counterpart of 説, a variant of 說. In the traditional graph, 言 is the speech-related element and 兌 is identified as the sound element.

formation.text: The traditional graph 說 is analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 言 contributes the speech-related meaning, while 兌 is identified as a sound element. The simplified graph 说 uses 讠, the left-side form of 言, and 兑, the simplified form of 兌. Current readings offer a comparison, but do not establish the historical sound relation.

components.text: 讠 is the left-side form of 言, the speech-related semantic element in traditional 說. The simplified-character standard identifies 讠 as a simplified radical used on the left; this supports a positional full-form relationship to 言.

兑 is the simplified form of traditional 兌, identified as the sound element in 說. Local Unihan kMandarin data gives 兑 duì and 说 shuō; the historical role is recorded in dictionaries, but this modern pair does not establish the earlier sound relation.

sound_limitation.text: Baxter–Sagart 2014 gives 兑 *lˤot-s and traditional 説 *l̥ot-s for “exhort.” Although these forms resemble one another within the same reconstruction system, the distinct glosses and readings do not independently establish 兑’s historical phonetic role or a sound derivation. The dictionary analysis identifies that role, but the sound comparison does not independently verify it.

sound.text: Local Unihan kMandarin data gives 兑 duì and 说 shuō. This modern Mandarin comparison does not establish the historical sound relation.

history.text: The traditional dictionary analysis writes 說 as 从言、兌 and identifies 兌 as phonetic; its glosses include explaining or releasing and, separately, discussion. A modern seal-style drawing of 說 illustrates this recorded analysis but is not an ancient artifact or evidence of the graph’s earliest form.

The standardized list gives 说〔説〕 and uses 讠 as a simplified left-side form for 言. 説 is also recorded as a variant of 說. Together these records support 说 as a simplified counterpart of 說, without establishing a dated sequence among the forms.

uncertainties.text: The earliest graphic attestation of 說 remains unresolved; proposed Warring States Chu forms are secondary reports rather than a confirmed earliest sequence.

Historical dictionaries identify 兌 as phonetic, but the supplied sound comparisons do not independently establish that role. No independent evidence establishes a semantic contribution from 兌; the additional semantic reading is a historical commentator’s interpretation.

The earliest attested uses of the spoken senses and their chronology are unresolved. Recorded examples include discussion, explanation, reporting, admonishing, persuasion, and joy, but do not establish a sequence of semantic developments.

Proposed word-family and Proto-Sino-Tibetan explanations for readings of the traditional character are competing hypotheses; the supplied evidence does not settle them or establish a semantic path among the senses.

senses.text: The character is used with the meanings “speak,” “say,” and “talk.” No securely dated earliest occurrence is established, so these meanings are not identified as the earliest attested sense.
The traditional dictionary account records uses meaning “explain” and “discuss”; it does not establish their chronological relationship to speaking or saying.
The traditional graph is recorded in admonishing and persuasion contexts. Their chronology relative to other senses is unresolved.
The character is also glossed “scold” and “upbraid”; no chronology or development from another sense is established.

limitations.text: The supplied evidence does not establish a dated earliest occurrence or a semantic sequence linking speaking, explaining, discussing, admonishing, persuasion, and scolding.
